Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book insights:

- The Beige Book around this period reported modest overall growth but a deceleration heading into winter as COVID-19 cases surged, with renewed disruptions to producers and shippers. Consumer spending softened, and leisure/hospitality remained notably weak. Employment gains slowed, with some renewed layoffs/furloughs, while wage and price pressures were modest to moderate and uneven.
- Housing activity stayed strong—consistent with the FOMC’s ongoing Treasury and agency MBS purchases—while manufacturing expanded but faced supply chain constraints and rising input costs. Small businesses reported more acute stress and uncertainty.
- Credit conditions were mixed but tighter at the margin for many firms, aligning with the SLOOS evidence of broad-based tightening in C&I, CRE, and riskier consumer credit. This suggests the bank lending channel is not fully amplifying policy accommodation, reinforcing the FOMC’s emphasis on considerable virus-driven downside risks.

Net effect: Beige Book corroborates uneven, slowing momentum and sectoral fragility despite supportive policy and strong housing. Relative to the prior SLOOS-informed read, this nudges the tone slightly more negative.
